family.template_used: not the listed family template -- recovered instead from the direct caller Shop_CompletePurchase (games/gs1/src/shop/complete_purchase.c) and the sibling item-slot decoder 080a9aec.c

domain: Called as Func_080b1868(unit_id, slot) from Shop_CompletePurchase after an item purchase is placed in a party unit's item slot. Reads the unit's item-slot u16 (id in the low 9 bits, a lock flag at 0x200); if locked, returns 0. Looks up the item's info, confirms the unit can equip it, finds any item it would replace and blocks the swap if that old item is unsellable, shows a Yes/No equip-confirmation message, and on confirmation equips the item, plays an equip fanfare and waits for it to finish if the item is flagged for one, then shows a closing message and returns 1 (so the caller sells the replaced item).
notes: The listed family template (08091c7c, a UI-wait/window-management owner) shares only coarse shape (object lookup, WaitFrames loop, message dispatch) and was not a useful line-by-line template. The direct caller Shop_CompletePurchase (`if (Func_080b1868(unit_id, added_slot) != 0) Shop_SellReplacedItem(...)`) fixed the real signature, and 080a9aec.c (`value & 0x200` lock bit / `value & 0x1ff` item id / `Func_08077018(id)[2]` kind byte) fixed the item-slot encoding and the AbilityInfo-style lookup shape, both already-established local idioms.

One deliberate asymmetry preserved from the assembly: the first Func_08077018 lookup (on the newly placed item) is called with the id explicitly masked to `& 0x1ff`, but the second lookup (on the replaced item, only reached when replaced != -1) is called with the raw unmasked u16 slot value -- the two call sites are not symmetric in the reference and the candidate reproduces that exactly.

The former allocation/scheduling diagnosis was false. The reference reloads the encoded inventory slot after Func_08077018, uses a separate old-item offset carrier, continues only when Func_080b0634 returns zero, checks UI completion before the first wait, and consumes Func_08015038 as an s32-returning interface. Restoring those source semantics eliminates the entire register residual under canonical flags; no compiler override or forced register is involved.
